\[
(t_1, \dots, t_{M-1}) = \arg\max \sum_{k=1}^{M} \omega_k (\mu_k - \mu)^2,
\qquad
M = 3
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(t_j\): The thresholds
- \(\omega_k, \mu_k\): The share and mean gray level of class k
- \(M\): The number of classes

The histogram of the luma is split by M - 1 thresholds into M classes. Class k has the share omega_k of the pixels and the mean gray level mu_k, and mu is the mean of the whole image. The thresholds are those that make the variance between the classes largest, as Otsu did for two classes. Liao and coworkers showed how to compute this quickly with lookup tables, but the search still tries every set of thresholds, so its cost grows fast with M. A pixel belongs to class c when its gray level is above exactly c thresholds. A level equal to a threshold belongs to the class below, as in Otsu's method. The classes are not split into connected parts, so one class can have many separate pieces.
